extracted.intended_audience: Authors/researchers submitting to Nature Portfolio journals, institutional press offices, and journalists covering Nature Portfolio content
extracted.subtask_description: Policies governing communication with the media, distribution of press releases, embargo timing, and handling of preprints/conference presentations for Nature Portfolio journals (as presented on the Nature Computational Science policy page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of direct solicitation of media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. Refer to the 'Communications between scientists' section for embargo policy as it pertains to conference presentations and preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-issued press releases and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature produces and distributes press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover, and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors. They receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material (for example, an accompanying News and Views article, and any extra images provided by the authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo on press release content
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and others must respect the stated embargo time/date. Press-release material provided in advance is password-protected and intended for registered journalists under the embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting of especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may therefore receive calls or emails from the media during this time; they are encouraged to cooperate with journalists so that media coverage of their work is accurate and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-arranged publicity must adhere to embargo and coordinate with press office
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must strictly adhere to Nature's media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with the Nature press office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of premature release to media
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release to the media denies journalists the confidence given by peer review and removes journalists' ability to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Portfolio policy frames embargoes as serving scientists, authors, journalists and the public by providing fair and equal access to complete and final versions of papers; authors should avoid releasing results prematurely to the media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for embargo breaches by journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Portfolio will continue to use removal from the press-release circulation list (and similar sanctions) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support open communications between researchers whether on a recognised community preprint server or preprint commenting platforms, through discussions at research meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission; exposure of preprints does not preempt submission. See linked policy pages for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for researchers/responding to media about preprints or conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission, but may reduce or pre-empt coverage by other media at the time of publication. Researchers approached by reporters about a preprint should make it clear that the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and that the conclusions may change. Authors are expected to keep details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should label preprints as provisional/not peer-reviewed so audiences understand the status of the findings.
